recent_posts.title: Databricks Academy Pro offers unlimited AI and data training for enterprise teams
recent_posts.summary: Databricks is launching Databricks Academy Pro, an annual per-seat subscription offering unlimited self-paced courses, live instructor-led training, hands-on labs, and certification vouchers — all within a real Databricks environment. The announcement is framed around the argument that workforce upskilling, not tooling, is the primary barrier to enterprise AI adoption. Citing Deloitte and BCG research, the post argues that continuous, team-wide training yields compounding AI returns, and that one-time training events are insufficient given the pace of platform and AI evolution. Three subscription tiers (Starter, Growth, Enterprise) unlock progressively more features including custom portals, community access, and dedicated program managers.

recent_posts.title: Rethinking Distributed Systems for Serverless Performance and Reliability
recent_posts.summary: Databricks explains the architectural decisions behind their serverless Spark compute platform, focusing on three core systems: Spark Connect, a smart workload gateway, and an adaptive autoscaler. Spark Connect replaces the monolithic Spark driver model with a client-server gRPC architecture, isolating user applications from compute and enabling multi-tenant stability. The gateway routes workloads by evaluating query size, cluster utilization, and latency profile to prevent resource contention. The autoscaler dynamically adjusts VM size and count, including automatic recovery from out-of-memory errors. Together these systems deliver measurable results: 99.998% upgrade success rate across 2 billion workloads, and customer outcomes like CKDelta reducing job times from 4-5 hours to 20 minutes and Unilever cutting operational costs by 25%.

recent_posts.title: How nOps Rebuilt Their Cloud Optimization Platform on Databricks Lakebase, and Why Other ISVs Should Too
recent_posts.summary: nOps, a cloud cost optimization platform managing $4B+ in annual cloud spend, migrated from a split architecture (Databricks Lakehouse + separate Postgres) to Databricks Lakebase, a fully managed PostgreSQL database natively integrated with the Lakehouse. The migration eliminated ETL sync pipelines, unified governance under Unity Catalog, and simplified their stack. The post outlines why other ISVs facing the same OLTP-meets-analytics tension should consider the same move, highlighting benefits like Postgres compatibility, scale-to-zero pricing, and reduced operational overhead.

recent_posts.title: The foundation of AI scalability: one team, one platform, one operating model
recent_posts.summary: Albertsons Companies, operating ~2,300 stores with $80B in revenue, shares how it moved from fragmented AI experiments to a centralized AI core. The strategy follows a 'franchise model': common infrastructure, governance, and reusable accelerators at the center, with local innovation at the edges. Built on Databricks, the platform covers data engineering, ML, governance, and analytics. Four strategic AI bets — customer experience, merchandising intelligence, labor, and supply chain — focus the work. In 9 months, engineers accepted 1.38 million lines of AI-generated code with 90%+ adoption. Non-technical teams get low-code dashboards and drag-and-drop agentic tools. KPIs now track reuse rates, time to deployment, responsible AI compliance, and business outcomes tied to AI uplift.

recent_posts.title: The Federal Data Paradox: Rich in Data, Poor in Access
recent_posts.summary: Federal agencies have invested heavily in data infrastructure, yet most decision-makers still rely on data teams to answer basic questions, creating a bottleneck. Databricks Genie is presented as a natural language interface that lets non-technical staff like program managers and policy analysts query agency data directly in plain language, while respecting existing access controls and governance policies. The post frames this as closing the 'last mile' of federal data modernization required by the Foundations for Evidence-Based Policymaking Act.

recent_posts.title: Model Risk Governance Is Not the Same as Risk Intelligence
recent_posts.summary: Banks have invested heavily in model risk governance frameworks, but risk leaders still struggle to get fast, fluid answers from their risk data. There's a gap between having governance infrastructure and having actionable risk intelligence. Databricks AI/BI Genie is presented as a solution that lets CROs and risk leaders query their risk data environment in natural language, with appropriate access controls and audit logging, enabling them to ask ad-hoc questions rather than relying on pre-built dashboards.

recent_posts.title: Unlocking SAP Business Context in Databricks with Semantic Metadata Delta Sharing
recent_posts.summary: SAP Business Data Cloud now automatically syncs semantic metadata and governance tags into Databricks Unity Catalog when SAP data products are shared via Delta Sharing. This means cryptic SAP table and column names like VBAK and KUNNR are enriched with business-friendly display names, descriptions, and primary/foreign key relationships directly in Unity Catalog. The sync also includes PersonalData governance tags for compliance and access control. The result is that Databricks AI tools like AI/BI Genie and the AI Assistant can immediately understand SAP data relationships, enabling natural language queries and accurate join-ready SQL without manual data dictionaries or tribal knowledge mapping.

recent_posts.title: The marketing activation gap has a fix: Databricks and Stitch partner to turn data infrastructure into marketing performance
recent_posts.summary: Databricks and Stitch are announcing a partnership aimed at closing the gap between enterprise data infrastructure and marketing execution. Many organizations have invested heavily in Databricks for data engineering but marketing teams remain disconnected from that infrastructure, relying on fragmented tool stacks. Stitch positions itself as a specialist partner with expertise in both Databricks and enterprise marketing operations, helping bridge the two. The partnership targets five areas of integration and is aimed at brands looking to modernize their marketing architecture with AI at the center.

recent_posts.title: Backstage with Lakebase
recent_posts.summary: Databricks Lakebase is a serverless Postgres-compatible database built on Neon's copy-on-write architecture, living inside the Databricks platform. This post documents migrating Backstage (Spotify's Internal Developer Portal) from standard Postgres/RDS to Lakebase, focusing on how instant database branching transforms the developer workflow. Key findings: a 63 MB database clone completes in 1.09 seconds, point-in-time recovery runs in under 4 seconds, and branches are fully isolated. The post argues that when database branching becomes as cheap as git branching, teams can eliminate mock objects (which account for 20-30% of test code), avoid staging collisions, and catch schema migration issues during development rather than at deployment. A VS Code/Cursor extension to auto-sync git and database branches is in development.

recent_posts.title: Approximate Answers, Exact Decisions: New Sketch Functions for Analytics
recent_posts.summary: Databricks introduces four new sketch function families powered by Apache DataSketches: KLL quantile sketches for fast percentile queries, Theta sketches for set operations on distinct values, Approximate Top-K for trending item detection, and Tuple sketches for combined distinct counting with metric aggregation. These replace expensive exact computations (global sorts, full shuffles) with bounded-memory approximations offering 1-2% configurable relative error and orders-of-magnitude speedups. Sketches can be built once during ETL, stored in Delta tables, and merged on read — enabling dashboards and trend analysis without rescanning raw data. Exact computation remains recommended for financial auditing and compliance use cases.

top_posts.title: How agentic software development will change databases
top_posts.summary: Agentic software development is reshaping database requirements in three key ways: evolutionary branching (agents create and discard database branches rapidly, with some projects reaching 500+ iterations), scale-to-zero economics (half of agentic app databases have compute lifetimes under 10 seconds, making fixed-cost databases unviable), and openness (agents trained on open-source ecosystems like Postgres operate more reliably with open interfaces and storage formats). Databricks's Lakebase addresses these needs with O(1) copy-on-write branching, sub-second scale-to-zero elasticity, and open Postgres page format storage on cloud object storage. A telling data point: AI agents in Lakebase now create roughly 4x more databases than human users.

top_posts.title: Building Custom LLM Judges for AI Agent Accuracy
top_posts.summary: MLflow introduces three new capabilities for evaluating AI agents: Tunable Judges for creating custom LLM evaluators using natural language instructions, Agent-as-a-Judge for automatically identifying relevant trace data without manual parsing, and Judge Builder for visual judge management with domain expert feedback. These tools enable teams to build domain-specific evaluation criteria, align judges with human feedback through continuous tuning, and scale quality assessment from prototype to production. The make_judge SDK simplifies creating custom judges, while alignment optimization incorporates subject matter expert feedback to improve evaluation accuracy over time.

top_posts.title: The New Way to Build Pipelines on Databricks: Introducing the IDE for Data Engineering
top_posts.summary: Databricks launched the IDE for Data Engineering in Public Preview, a dedicated development environment for building declarative data pipelines within the Databricks Workspace. The IDE provides an integrated experience with features like automatic dependency graph visualization, file-based dataset organization, built-in data previews, debugging tools, and Git integration. It supports the declarative programming paradigm where developers specify what they want to achieve rather than how to build it, with the editor handling execution planning and optimization. The tool consolidates pipeline authoring, testing, version control, and scheduling into a single interface, aiming to improve developer productivity and reduce context switching.

top_posts.title: Introducing Apache Spark 4.0
top_posts.summary: Apache Spark 4.0 introduces key advancements in SQL language, Python support, structured streaming, and usability, enhancing big data processing. Notable features include improved multi-language compatibility, new SQL scripting capabilities, enhanced Python APIs, and structured logging. This release offers greater modularity, scalability, and standards compliance, making it future-ready for large-scale data analytics.

top_posts.title: Introducing Kasal
top_posts.summary: Kasal is a new visual, no-code platform built on Databricks for designing, deploying, and monitoring agentic AI workflows. It uses a drag-and-drop canvas or conversational assistant to let both technical and non-technical users build single and multi-agent systems without writing orchestration code. Under the hood it leverages CrewAI for agent orchestration and integrates with MLflow for tracing, Databricks Apps for deployment, and supports MCP servers, Genie, and custom APIs. Workflows can be exported as code for further customization, and a catalog enables reuse across teams.
